newsitem.title: USA: Philip Morris to remove cigarette sign in Atlanta.
newsitem.headline: Philip Morris to remove cigarette sign in Atlanta.

text.p: Philip Morris has agreed to remove a billboard advertising Marlboro cigarettes after the Atlanta Braves play their last home game of the baseball season Monday night, the Justice Department said.

It charged that the sign had been placed in left-centre field in such a way that it appeared on telecasts of baseball games, in violation of a federal law banning cigarette advertising on television. It said it had received complaints about the Marlboro sign appearing on several telecasts of the baseball team's games this season.

Department officials told the cigarette manufacturer and Atlanta-Fulton County Stadium the sign violated the advertising ban and a court agreement reached with Philip Morris last year. Philip Morris agreed to take down the sign at the end of the regular season but did not admit that it violated the law or the consent decree, the officials said.
The company late last year removed a second and more conspicuous Marlboro sign and has taken down a number of signs at other professional sports stadiums around the country as part of the agreement.
